Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: payment data-flow diagram may not reflect all current integrations and connected systems.
Potential Business Impact: Scope omission can leave relevant systems outside security governance and testing.
Required Validation: Reconcile approved diagrams with actual payment flows, inventories, network paths and provider responsibilities.
Proposed Treatment: Confirm CDE boundaries; update diagrams and inventories; obtain accountable approval.
Closure Criteria: Approved current diagrams and inventory reconcile to validated environment; scope decision documented.

Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: network security rules may lack current business justification or periodic review evidence.
Potential Business Impact: Unnecessary connectivity may increase attack paths into or out of the CDE.
Required Validation: Inspect actual rules, review records, tickets and approved data flows.
Proposed Treatment: Remove obsolete rules; document business need and owners; establish periodic review.
Closure Criteria: Sampled rules are approved, justified, current and retested.

Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: secure configuration evidence may be incomplete for some in-scope components.
Potential Business Impact: Weak or inconsistent settings may expose systems to compromise.
Required Validation: Sample in-scope assets and compare configuration evidence to approved baselines.
Proposed Treatment: Remediate deviations; maintain baseline and exception register.
Closure Criteria: Sampled assets meet approved baselines or have authorized, tracked exceptions.

Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: account-data storage and retention decisions may not be fully evidenced.
Potential Business Impact: Unnecessary or inadequately protected data retention may increase breach impact and obligations.
Required Validation: Confirm actual storage locations, data types, retention rules and protection; never copy live card data into portfolio evidence.
Proposed Treatment: Minimize retention; apply required protections; securely remove prohibited/unneeded data under approved procedures.
Closure Criteria: Data inventory and retention decisions are approved and verified; relevant controls are tested.

Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: vulnerability remediation and secure-change records may not consistently show end-to-end closure.
Potential Business Impact: Known weaknesses or unreviewed changes may remain exploitable.
Required Validation: Sample vulnerabilities and changes; trace through approval, fix, retest and closure evidence.
Proposed Treatment: Define remediation SLAs and secure change gates; track exceptions and retest.
Closure Criteria: Samples demonstrate required handling, approvals and validated closure.

Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: access reviews or MFA evidence may not cover every applicable privileged access path.
Potential Business Impact: Unauthorized or excessive access may enable account-data compromise.
Required Validation: Review actual access paths, identities, effective permissions, MFA configuration and lifecycle evidence.
Proposed Treatment: Remove unjustified access; enforce applicable authentication controls; strengthen periodic review.
Closure Criteria: All sampled access meets requirements or approved exception process; retest evidence retained.

Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: logs may lack documented coverage, review ownership or response evidence.
Potential Business Impact: Delayed detection and incomplete investigation records may increase incident impact.
Required Validation: Inspect log source coverage, access protections, review records and alert response tickets.
Proposed Treatment: Close coverage gaps; assign review owners; test alerts and escalation.
Closure Criteria: Required sources are logged and protected; reviews and responses are evidenced.

Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: security testing or segmentation evidence may be outdated or incomplete.
Potential Business Impact: Weaknesses in CDE defenses or scope-reduction assumptions may go undetected.
Required Validation: Inspect current test scope, dates, findings, segmentation boundaries and remediation/retest evidence.
Proposed Treatment: Perform required testing with authorized qualified resources; remediate and retest findings.
Closure Criteria: Applicable testing is completed, findings are tracked and closure/segmentation conclusions are evidenced.

Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: service-provider responsibilities or compliance monitoring may not be fully documented.
Potential Business Impact: Gaps between merchant and provider responsibilities may leave controls unmanaged.
Required Validation: Inspect contracts, responsibility matrix, provider evidence, review records and owners.
Proposed Treatment: Maintain provider inventory, verify evidence scope and document shared responsibilities.
Closure Criteria: Current provider evidence and responsibility allocation are reviewed and approved.

Illustrative Gap Hypothesis: Illustrative only: gaps may not have consistent owners, due dates, retest evidence and approval.
Potential Business Impact: Weak closure discipline can allow recurring or unaccepted risk to persist.
Required Validation: Sample tickets and risk acceptance records; trace requirement-to-fix-to-retest.
Proposed Treatment: Standardize remediation workflow and management escalation.
Closure Criteria: Every material gap has an owner, due date, closure evidence and authorized final disposition.
